extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, publishers, and editorial office staff
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of COPE guidelines intended to advise editors, publishers, and researchers on expected publication-ethics practices across editorial processes, peer review, authorship, retractions, and relationships with societies. The page lists multiple standalone guideline topics with short summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics toolkit for a successful editorial office
rubrics_metrics.description: To help ensure the integrity of the scholarly record and the publication process, editorial offices should define and implement best practices in publication ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This COPE guide is a comprehensive toolkit that explains expected ethical practices in scholarly publishing, and highlights resources for editorial offices to develop their codes of ethical conduct and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing peer reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on expected practices and appropriate circumstances regarding the editing of peer reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidelines look at the need for journals to amend peer reviews, and provide insight into situations where this might be an appropriate course of action. Journals should have clear policies on editing peer reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial board participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of editorial board appointment and engagement, roles and responsibilities, and key details to consider during recruitment such as participation on multiple editorial boards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COPE Guidelines are formal COPE policy and are intended to advise editors and publishers on expected publication ethics practice; guidance includes considerations for appointment, engagement and members' responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing relationships between society-owned journals, their society, and publishers
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and relationship management for journals affiliated with learned societies or professional associations to ensure high-quality, ethically sound, and transparent arrangements among journals, publishers, and societies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regardless of publication arrangements and number of affiliated journals, relationships and policies must be of the highest quality, ethically sound, and as transparent as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Transparency and Best Practice in Scholarly Publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint principles from COPE, DOAJ, OASPA, and WAME outlining transparency and best practices for scholarly publishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These principles set expectations for transparency in publishing operations and best-practice standards for journals and publishers (consortium guidance referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Journals’ Best Practices for ensuring consent for publishing medical case reports
rubrics_metrics.description: General principles around consent and consent forms for editors to use when developing forms for their journals' purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides guidance for editors on consent requirements and template/forms development to ensure patient consent is appropriately obtained and documented for case reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing of information among editors-in-chief regarding possible misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on editors-in-chief sharing information about suspected misconduct to preserve the integrity of the scientific record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sharing information can help EICs of affected journals conduct investigations with greater efficiency and effectiveness; the guidelines discuss when and how such sharing is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text recycling guidelines for editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on expected practice when identifying sections of the same text appearing in more than one of an author's own publications (text recycling/self-plagiarism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to advise editors and publishers on how to identify, evaluate, and respond to instances of recycled text across submissions and published work.

rubrics_metrics.name: A short guide to ethical editing for new editors
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise summary of key principles, tasks and relationships of the journal editor role to assist new editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to summarise key principles and relationships; useful for editors working alone or new to the role who may encounter different processes and systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for Editors: research, audit and service evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on regulations regarding what type of study requires ethical approval and how journals should handle submissions of studies that may not satisfy local requirements for independent ethical approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains variation in ethical approval requirements worldwide and how misunderstandings can lead to rejection; advises editors on assessing ethical approval and submission suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical guidelines for peer reviewers (English)
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic principles and standards to which all peer reviewers should adhere during the peer review process in research publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to be applied across disciplines; highlights reviewers' ethical obligations, and that many reviewers come to the role unaware of these duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation between research institutions and journals on research integrity cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on the complementary duties of institutions and journals relating to research and publication misconduct and how they should cooperate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions are responsible for researcher conduct and healthy research environments; journals are responsible for editor conduct, safeguarding the research record, and ensuring reliability of published material; guidance discusses cooperation processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice for editors on when a retraction should be considered, what to include in a notice, how quickly to issue a retraction, who should issue a retraction, and how to handle inconclusive evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COPE's Retraction guidelines provide structured advice on timing, content, responsibility, and handling ambiguous cases in issuing retractions to preserve the integrity of the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to handle authorship disputes: a guide for new researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for new researchers on good authorship practice, and advice on how to deal with authorship issues as they arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides practical advice aimed at early-career researchers about authorship expectations and dispute resolution approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for the Board of Directors of Learned Society Journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance incorporated into COPE materials regarding governance for boards overseeing society journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers recommendations for the Board of Directors of learned society journals; incorporated into broader COPE guidance on managing society–publisher relationships.
